query: Which material can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward HER and HOR, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Pt–Ni core–shell nanoparticles will exhibit enhanced catalytic activity and durability for both HER and HOR compared to pure Pt catalysts.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional pure platinum nanoparticles used as catalysts in standard electrochemical cells.
generation.intervention: Synthesize core–shell nanoparticles having a Ni-rich core and an ultrathin Pt surface (Pt-skin) layer.
generation.conditions: Electrochemical testing in acidic media (e.g., 0.5 M H2SO4) under standard HER and HOR operation conditions, including cyclic voltammetry and durability cycling.
generation.structural_mediator: The core–shell architecture, where the Ni core modulates the electronic properties of the Pt-skin, alters the hydrogen adsorption energy.
generation.mechanism: The Ni core induces a downshift in the Pt d-band center, leading to a bonding environment that weakens hydrogen adsorption just enough to optimize reaction kinetics. Simultaneously, the protective Pt-skin enhances corrosion resistance and durability.
generation.predicted_outcome: Lower overpotentials and increased exchange current densities for HER and HOR, along with slower performance degradation during accelerated durability tests compared to pure Pt catalysts.
generation.baseline: Electrodes using pure Pt nanoparticles under identical operating conditions.
generation.boundary: The benefits are expected primarily in acidic environments; variations in the Pt:Ni ratio, particle size, and operating conditions (e.g., switching to alkaline electrolytes) may affect the performance improvements.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal core–shell configuration (e.g., precise Pt-skin thickness and Ni core composition) and long-term stability under real-world cycling are uncertain and require further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of catalyst electrodes: one set using Pt–Ni core–shell nanoparticles and another set using pure Pt nanoparticles. Under controlled conditions in 0.5 M H2SO4, measure HER and HOR activities by cyclic voltammetry and perform prolonged durability testing (e.g., continuous potential cycling or chronoamperometry).
measurements: Overpotential at a fixed current density
Electrochemical Surface Area (ECSA) loss or degradation rate over time
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Pt–Ni core–shell catalysts do not show statistically significant (beyond experimental error) improvements in catalytic activity (reduced overpotential, increased exchange current density) and durability (slower ECSA loss or performance degradation) compared to pure Pt catalysts, then the hypothesis is falsified.
